visual: Small, dense, bushy evergreen shrub with an upright habit and unusually tiny dark green leaves neatly margined creamy white, creating a fine-textured variegated appearance.
water: Water regularly during establishment. Once established, water during prolonged dry periods while allowing excess moisture to drain freely.
soil: Moist but well-drained or well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral and alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently waterlogged soil. Variegated foliage generally develops its strongest colour in good light.
prune: Prune as required to maintain shape and density. Remove damaged, reverted or unwanted shoots.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten. Wear gloves and protective equipment when handling.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most places throughout the UK, approximately -15 to -10°C.
resilience: Hardy, evergreen and tolerant of a wide range of soils and aspects once established.
uses: Low hedging, edging, containers, courtyard gardens, coastal gardens, ground cover and mixed borders.
foliage: Evergreen; very small dark green leaves edged creamy white.
container: Excellent compact evergreen for containers and formal clipped displays.
uncertain: Also encountered under the synonym Euonymus japonicus 'Microphyllus Variegatus'.
peak "Year-round foliage" converted to "Jan-Dec" to parse as Mon-Mon.

visual: Compact bulbous perennial forming a mound of dramatic three-part triangular leaves in rich purple to burgundy tones. Slender stems carry delicate pale pink to whitish-purple funnel-shaped flowers above the foliage, while the leaves characteristically fold closed at night.
water: Keep moderately moist during active growth but never waterlogged. Allow the surface of the compost to begin drying between waterings and reduce watering significantly during dormancy.
aspect: Bright indirect light to partial shade; sheltered
soil: Humus-rich or sandy, moist but well-drained soil or free-draining houseplant compost; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogging and intense scorching sunlight. Growth may naturally die back during dormancy; reduce watering until new growth resumes.
prune: No routine pruning required. Remove dead or yellowing foliage and spent flower stems as necessary.
toxicity: Oxalis contains oxalates and should not be eaten in quantity; keep ornamental houseplants away from pets prone to chewing foliage.
hardinessNote: RHS rates 'Mijke' H3, approximately -5 to 1°C. In the UK it is commonly grown as a houseplant or protected container plant and should be protected from hard frost.
resilience: Easy to maintain under protected conditions and capable of entering dormancy before producing fresh growth again.
uses: Houseplants, conservatories, greenhouse displays, patio containers, hanging baskets and sheltered summer displays.
foliage: Deciduous or seasonally dormant; clover-like leaves divided into three triangular rich purple leaflets which fold in low light and at night.
container: Excellent container and houseplant; the supplied P12 designation indicates a 12 cm nursery pot rather than part of the cultivar name.
uncertain: 'Ikigai' is a commercial marketing concept/range associated with this plant, while RHS accepts the cultivar as Oxalis triangularis 'Mijke'. P12 denotes the 12 cm pot size rather than a botanical name.
